correctness.rationale: Conditioning on the difference of the two-coin sums gives the exact autocorrelation expression. Direct expansion yields derivative \(4Dr-2Ds+2G\) and second derivative \(4D\), while \(2D\) is the squared \(\ell_2\)-norm of the zero-extended second-difference sequence, hence positive for every nonzero finite-support probability mass function. The feasible product interval at fixed sum is exactly the stated interval, so strict convexity makes the projection formula necessary and sufficient. Specializing to the empty background gives \(D=3\), \(G=1\), and the two boundary equations produce the thresholds \(1/3\) and \(1-1/\sqrt3\). The inspected exact-rational verifier independently reconstructs convolutions, the energy identity, the quadratic completion, projection, and the two-coin phase partition; those finite checks corroborate the symbolic proof.

final_claim: For an independent finite-support integer-valued background and two Bernoulli variables with fixed sum, the order-two collision probability is a strictly convex quadratic in their product with curvature given by the squared second-difference energy of the background law, so the entropy maximizer is the projection of one explicit stationary product onto the feasible interval; for two coins this yields the stated deterministic, unequal, and balanced phases with balancing optimal exactly when \(|s-1|\le 1/\sqrt3\).
